datasets.title: Satellite detected water extent in South of Ghat City, Ghat Governorate, South Province, Libya as of 18 August 2024
datasets.description: UNOSAT code: FL20240812LBY This map illustrates satellite-detected water extent in Ghat City, Ghat Governorate, South Province, Libya as observed from a WorldView-3 satellite image acquired on 18 August 2024 at 11:53 local time (09:53 UTC). Within analysed area of about 35km², a total of about 4 km² of land appears to be affected by floodwaters. UNITAR-UNOSAT identified 49 potentially affected structures within the analysed area. This is a preliminary analysis and has not yet been validated in the field. Please send ground feedback to the United Nations Satellite Centre (UNOSAT). [Source: This metadata record was automatically extracted from the Humanitarian Data Exchange (HDX); Original dataset: https://data.humdata.org/dataset/water-extent-in-south-of-ghat-city-ghat-governorate-south-province-libya-as-of-18-august-2]
datasets.details: This is a preliminary assessment and has not yet been validated in the field. It is important to consider the characteristics of the source imagery used in the analyses when interpreting results. For damage assessments it should be noted that only significant damage to the structural integrity of the buildings analyzed can be seen in imagery, while minor damage such as cracks or holes may not be visible at all. For flood extractions using radar data it is important to note that urban areas and highly vegetated areas may mask the flood signature and result in underestimation of flood waters. Users with specific questions or concerns should contact unosat@unitar.org to seek clarification.

lineage.description: WorldView-3 satellite imagery acquired on 18 August 2024 was analyzed by UNOSAT analysts to detect water extent through visual interpretation and comparison with baseline imagery. Satellite-detected floodwaters covering approximately 4 km² were mapped as vector polygons, and 49 potentially affected building structures were identified within the 35 km² study area.
